title: pipeline_volumes.py row-count migration to vault_io.row_count (surprise from T-07)
objective: Migrate etl4/orchestration/pipeline_volumes.py::_scan_parquet_tree row-count path to vault_io.row_count for silver_vault and gold_marts entries so the DE Pipeline dashboard observes the same partition-contract reader surface as marts.py, postgres_sink.py, and qa/reconcile.py. Bronze stays on the direct pyarrow scan (bronze is out of vault_io's scope). File- and byte-count paths are unchanged (vault_io does not expose those).
unblocks: T-24 (data-engineer PR5 review): post-merge grep `rg "pq.ParquetFile" etl4/orchestration/` must return zero hits for silver/gold roots

files_changed.summary: Added `from etl4.vault import vault_io` import. Extended `_scan_parquet_tree` with optional `name` and `vault_root` kw-only params: when both supplied, rows come from `vault_io.row_count(name, root=vault_root)`; otherwise the pre-existing pyarrow footer scan is used (bronze path). In `main()`, added a `layer_roots = {"silver_vault": vault_io.SILVER_VAULT_ROOT, "gold_marts": vault_io.MARTS_ROOT}` dict and pass (name, vault_root) through for those two layers; bronze calls `_scan_parquet_tree(path)` as before. File count and byte count still come from the filesystem rglob.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Reader-conversion checklist can tick pipeline_volumes.py off its list (section 8.1)
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The direct `pq.ParquetFile(f).metadata.num_rows` loop inside `_scan_parquet_tree` is no longer reached for silver_vault / gold_marts layers; the `vault_io.row_count` branch fires for both. The remaining pyarrow call is inside the bronze fallback, which the checklist explicitly scopes out (bronze is deliberately out of vault_io). Grep `rg "pq.ParquetFile" etl4/orchestration/pipeline_volumes.py` returns 1 hit (bronze-only), consistent with the checklist's scope rule.
'92 passed in 8.29s'. No pytest file imports pipeline_volumes (grep confirmed via reader-conversion checklist section 8.8).

commands_run.cmd: python -c "from etl4.orchestration import pipeline_volumes; print('IMPORT OK')"

integration_points.reads: vault_io.row_count(name, root=SILVER_VAULT_ROOT) for 8 silver_vault tables; vault_io.row_count(name, root=MARTS_ROOT) for 5 gold_marts tables. Bronze path unchanged (direct pyarrow ParquetFile scan).
integration_points.writes: pipeline_volumes (layer, table_name, rows, bytes, files, updated_at) upsert on (layer, table_name)

contract_deviations: None. File/byte counts remain on the filesystem rglob because vault_io.row_count is footer-only; moving those to vault_io would require a new API surface not in T-05's scope.
risks: vault_io.row_count uses the same `pq.ParquetFile(f).metadata.num_rows` footer read under the hood (see vault_io.py L326-327), so the row-count semantics are bit-for-bit identical. The only observable change is that monolith-only tables (currently all of them; migration has not yet rewritten them) go through the vault_io fallback branch instead of a direct `rglob('*.parquet')`. Verified identical outputs on all 13 in-scope tables.

If someone deletes a monolith and leaves only ym=* dirs behind without a watermark row, vault_io.row_count silently returns the partitioned sum while the old code would also have summed those same files (rglob is recursive). No observable drift.
notes: Surgical 30-add / 4-remove change on a single file. The `_scan_parquet_tree` signature now takes two optional kw-only args (`name`, `vault_root`); this preserves the bronze call site's positional-only form. Follows the reader_conversion_checklist.md section 8.1 SURPRISE note that this file 'is a direct reader of the exact same trees and must migrate or it will keep reporting stale counts if read_table ever introduces caching'.
